title: streaming: add lifecycle controls for client cancel, disconnect, reconnect/resume and server timeouts
author: Asha Malik
description: Motivation: Streaming sessions were vulnerable to silent client disconnects, abrupt client cancels, and server-side timeouts which caused token duplication, KV cache corruption, and poor UX for reconnect/resume flows. This PR implements a set of lifecycle controls across the API surface: 1) explicit client CANCEL signal handling (HTTP/2 GRACEFUL_CLOSE and SSE close semantics) to mark streams as aborted and trigger server-side cleanup; 2) detect and persist resumable stream checkpoints (session id + KV cache pointer) so clients can reconnect and resume from last committed token; 3) robust disconnect detection and timeout config with per-session grace periods to avoid premature KV eviction under flakey networks; 4) unify behavior with OpenAI-compat layer so downstream SDKs (python/ts/go) get consistent semantics; 5) add server-side guardrails to avoid double-emit on reconnect races and to reconcile partial responses when a client reconnects. Changes include protocol-level updates, runtime scheduler integration, API contract additions, and test coverage. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-1189) - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Backwards-compatible defaults (resume disabled by default) - [x] SDK compatibility tests updated - [x] Metrics and tracing for lifecycle events added Backwards compatibility: defaults preserve current behavior (no resume) but improve signal handling so clients that close streams no longer leave behind orphaned sessions. Controlled rollouts: feature gated by runtime flag and an API header for preview. See release_notes for migration guidance.

review_comments: Jonah Rivera: "This looks good overall, but can we avoid a sync call during checkpoint commit on the hot path? Consider batching commits or making them async with at-least-once semantics."
Asha Malik: "Good point — switched to async commit with an in-memory buffer and background flush; added metrics to monitor buffer lag."
Priya Desai: "Can you clarify semantics for resume when model updates occur? We risk resuming into a different tokenizer/kv layout."
Asha Malik: "Added a session schema version and model-hash requirement: resume requires matching model-hash or will return 409 with a clear retry hint."
Luca Moretti: "Tests flaked on CI (integration/test_streaming_reconnect) on the first run — seems timing-sensitive. Recommend adding jitter to client reconnect to avoid deterministic race."
Asha Malik: "Added jitter and extended grace window in test harness. Reran CI and green."
Security review (internal): "Ensure resume tokens cannot be used to hijack other sessions. Auth header must be validated against session owner."
ci_checks: bench: warn (baseline latency +3ms under resume enabled)
release_notes: Improved streaming lifecycle: servers now correctly handle client cancel and disconnect signals, added an opt-in reconnect/resume mechanism with session checkpoints, and configurable server-side streaming timeouts/grace periods. Default behavior unchanged. Upgrade notes: SDKs should adopt the new X-Resume-Session header to opt into resume flows; services using custom reverse proxies should forward SSE close/graceful close signals. See docs/streaming-lifecycle.md for details.
